text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Local taxes expected to be lower in 1997.
-- CNPF employers' federation chairman Jean Gandois reaffirms call for a liberal economic policy.

-- British European commissioner Leon Brittan says in an interview foreign investors may avoid Britain if it does not take part in European monetary union, European Commissioner Neil Kinnock adds membership means increased negotiating power in world affairs.
-- Regional newspaper L'Est Republicain to buy Les Dernieres Nouvelles d'Alsace.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Ruling conservative coalition to unveil platform for parliamentary election today, expected to emphasise small and medium firms as the centre of its fight against unemployment.
-- Credit Immobilier still interested in bidding for Credit Foncier de France.
-- Public works remain a strategic activity for Bouygues, which also expects telecommunications activities to become profitable by the year 2001.
-- Insurer GAN posts a 5.7 billion francs loss for 1996.
-- Renault to manufacture Scenic cars in Brazil.
L'AGEFI

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis in an interview proposes to alter article 16 of the trade code to allow firms to hold their accounts and pay taxes and labour charges in francs or in euros from January 1, 1999. Says nothing indicates an overshooting of the state budget for 1997.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Alcatel Alsthom chairman Serge Tchuruk says in an interview the Thomson-CSF privatisation calendar must be respected, delays would jeopardise the European defence industry restructuring, he adds.

-- Forty two percent of people polled on April 26 and 27 by Le Figaro and Sofres trust the ruling coalition to give the country a new forward momentum, 55 percent remain skeptical. Fifty four percent think the socialist party is not ready to run the country.
-- Former Prime Minister Edouard Balladur calls for a liberal approach to economic policy.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Bouygues, returned to profit in 1996 with a 654 million franc result but loses ground against competitor Cie Generale des Eaux.
